title: A lifted compatible scheme atlas presents an infinitesimal space pushout
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and work with algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A thickening means a representable closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces; closed immersions are tested after scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the point topology is the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas. An affine morphism is representable with affine scheme base changes. Let $i:T\hookrightarrow T^+$ be a thickening, let $a:T\to S$ be affine, and let $P=S\amalg_T T^+$ be the algebraic-space pushout [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout]. Suppose $V,W$ are schemes with representable surjective etale morphisms $V\to S$, $W\to T^+$ and a specified isomorphism $V\times_S T\simeq W\times_{T^+}T$ over $T$. Put $D=V\times_S T$, a scheme affine over $V$, and use this isomorphism to define $D\to W$. Then the induced morphism $$V\amalg_D W\longrightarrow P$$ is representable surjective etale. The source is the scheme pushout [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout], and its map is the unique one extending $V\to S\to P$ and $W\to T^+\to P$. The spaces $T,T^+,S$ need not be schemes. There are no flatness, finite-presentation, separation, quasi-compactness or finite-order assumptions beyond the stated hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 07VX, lemma-pushout-along-thickening, construction of V\prime/R\prime with a chosen scheme atlas and its etale lift; Tag 07W0, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-over-pushout, and Tag 07W2, equation-cube-over, northeast atlas arrow.

proof.text: Write $Q=V\amalg_D W$. The specified overlap identifies $D\to W$ with the base change of $T\hookrightarrow T^+$, so it is a thickening by [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change]. By the definition of the representable affine map $a$, its base change $D\to V$ is an affine morphism of schemes. Thus [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout] constructs $Q$ and makes $V\hookrightarrow Q$ a thickening. Applied to this scheme span, [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout] says that the scheme pushout is also its algebraic-space pushout. Consequently there is a unique $q:Q\to P$ extending the two maps in the statement. We will construct a quotient of $Q$ which is another pushout of the original space span, and identify its atlas map with $q$.

Form the kernel pairs $R_V=V\times_S V$, $R_W=W\times_{T^+}W$, and $R_D=D\times_TD$. They are schemes, by the scheme-source fibre-product assertion of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Fibre-product associativity, with the prescribed overlap on both factors, gives
$$R_D\simeq R_V\times_ST\simeq R_W\times_{T^+}T.$$
Therefore $R_D\hookrightarrow R_W$ is a thickening by [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change], and $R_D\to R_V$ is affine by the scheme tests in the definition of $a$. Form $R=R_V\amalg_{R_D}R_W$ using [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]; it makes $R_V\hookrightarrow R$ a thickening. Both projections on the pieces agree over $R_D$ and induce maps $s,t:R\rightrightarrows Q$.

source.place: Tag 07VX, second paragraph, construction of the relation pushout.

proof.text:
For each of $s$ and $t$, the maps on pieces $R_V\to V$ and $R_W\to W$ are etale: they are scheme base changes of the given representable etale atlas maps, by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Their pullbacks to $D$ are the two corresponding projections $R_D\to D$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-infinitesimal-etale-patching] to the scheme span $V\leftarrow D\hookrightarrow W$ and this compatible etale triple. It makes $s,t$ etale and its canonical unit gives, for either projection,
$$R\times_Q V\simeq R_V,\qquad R\times_Q W\simeq R_W.$$
These are the projection-induced identifications, with the specified overlap, not merely abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 07VX, second paragraph, etale relation projections; schemes Tag 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), part (5).

proof.text:
The diagonals $V\to R_V$ and $W\to R_W$ agree over $D$ and glue by the scheme pushout to $e:Q\to R$, with $(s,t)e=\Delta_Q$. The flips on $R_V,R_W$ likewise glue to $i:R\to R$ with $(s,t)i=\mathrm{flip}\circ(s,t)$. Put $K=R\times_{t,Q,s}R$, with outer maps $s\mathrm{pr}_1,t\mathrm{pr}_2$. This is a scheme etale over $Q$ through $s\mathrm{pr}_1$: the first projection is a base change of the etale map $s$, and then compose with $s$, using [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Successively applying the projection-compatible identifications of step 3 gives
$$K\times_QV\simeq R_V\times_{t,V,s}R_V,\quad K\times_QW\simeq R_W\times_{t,W,s}R_W,$$
with overlap $R_D\times_{t,D,s}R_D$. For example, requiring the first source to lie in $V$ puts the first arrow in $R_V$ and its target in $V$; requiring this target to be the second source puts the second arrow in $R_V$. The argument for $W$ is identical with $R_W$. The canonical counit of [lem-sfb-scheme-infinitesimal-etale-patching] makes $K$ the scheme pushout of these two restrictions. Kernel-pair composition on them agrees on their overlap and therefore glues to $c:K\to R$. Its outer source and target equal $s\mathrm{pr}_1,t\mathrm{pr}_2$: check this on the two pushout pieces, where it is the kernel-pair formula. These are exactly the three operation identities required by [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation].

source.place: Tag 07VX, second paragraph, the omitted composition construction, supplied using the canonical etale counit of schemes Tag 07RX.

proof.text: For every algebraically closed field $k$ over $B$, the thickenings $V\hookrightarrow Q$ and $R_V\hookrightarrow R$ identify their $k$-valued points. Indeed locally their defining ideals are nil: a closed immersion with full underlying space has every defining element in every prime. Every map to a field kills these elements and so factors uniquely through the closed subscheme. Thus $(s,t):R(k)\to Q(k)^2$ is identified with the kernel relation $R_V(k)=V(k)\times_{S(k)}V(k)$. Its map is injective and its image is an equivalence relation. With step 3 and the operations of step 4, [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation] now proves that $(s,t)$ is a monomorphism defining an equivalence relation on all scheme tests. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]: its fppf sheaf quotient $F=Q/R$ is an algebraic space, and $p:Q\to F$ is representable surjective etale with the stated coequalizer universal property.

source.place: Tag 07VX, relation and quotient paragraph; groupoids.tex Tag 0DT7 (lemma-etale-equivalence-relation); spaces.tex Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation).

proof.text: The maps $V\to Q\xrightarrow{p}F$ and $W\to Q\xrightarrow{p}F$ coequalize $R_V$ and $R_W$, since these relations map to $R$ and $p s=p t$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], $S$ and $T^+$ are the sheafified quotients of precisely these two kernel pairs. The quotient universal property in [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] therefore descends the maps uniquely to $S\to F$ and $T^+\to F$. They agree on $T$: after its representable surjective etale cover $D\to T$ both are the map $D\to Q\to F$. This is a cover by base change of $V\to S$, as in [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; equality descends because $F$ is a sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. We have constructed a cocone of the original span, without assuming that its pushout map is etale.

source.place: Tag 07VX, paragraph constructing the maps to the quotient; spaces.tex Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation).

proof.text: Let $L/B$ be any algebraic space and let $u:S\to L$, $v:T^+\to L$ agree on $T$. Their maps from $V,W$ agree on $D$, so the algebraic-space pushout property of $Q$ in [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout] gives a unique $h:Q\to L$. The composites $hs,ht$ agree on $R_V$, since both there factor through $u$, and on $R_W$, since both there factor through $v$. The same node, applied to the scheme relation span $R_V\leftarrow R_D\hookrightarrow R_W$, says that $R$ is also an algebraic-space pushout. Hence $hs=ht$ on $R$. The coequalizer property of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives a unique $\bar h:F\to L$. Its restrictions are $u,v$, checked after the two atlases using [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation]. Conversely every map from $F$ supplies such a pair. If two maps supply the same pair, their composites with $p$ agree on $V,W$, hence on $Q$, hence they agree on $F$ by the same coequalizer property. Thus $F$ is the algebraic-space pushout of $S\leftarrow T\hookrightarrow T^+$.

source.place: Tag 07VX, final paragraph, universal property against arbitrary algebraic-space targets.

proof.text: Since $P$ and $F$ are pushouts of the same span, their universal properties give inverse maps $\alpha:F\to P$ and $\beta:P\to F$ fixing $S,T^+$. Each composite is the identity because it restricts to the identity on both pieces. The composite $\alpha p:Q\to P$ agrees with $q$ on $V$ and $W$, so it equals $q$ by the algebraic-space pushout property of $Q$. By [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], $p$ is representable surjective etale; [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] preserves this under composition with the isomorphism $\alpha$. Therefore $q$ is representable surjective etale, as asserted. The construction used arbitrary thickenings and the prescribed atlases throughout; none of the additional finiteness or separation hypotheses excluded in the statement was introduced.

source.place: Tag 07VX, quotient presentation followed by pushout uniqueness; Tag 07W2 (equation-cube-over), northeast atlas arrow.

lean.statement: theorem spacePushout_liftedAtlas {B : Scheme.{u}} (T T' S P : AlgebraicSpace B) (i : T ⟶ T') (a : T ⟶ S) (j : S ⟶ P) (b : T' ⟶ P) (hi : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom) (hiTop : IsHomeomorph (mapPoint i.hom.hom)) (ha : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsAffineHom p.left) a.hom.hom) (hP : IsPushout a i j b) (V W : Over B) (v : schemeSpace V ⟶ S) (w : schemeSpace W ⟶ T') (hv : IsEtale v.hom.hom) (hvSurj : IsSurjective v.hom.hom) (hw : IsEtale w.hom.hom) (hwSurj : IsSurjective w.hom.hom) (φ : Limits.pullback v.hom a.hom ≅ Limits.pullback w.hom i.hom) (hφ : φ.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.snd w.hom i.hom = Limits.pullback.snd v.hom a.hom) : ∃ (D : Over B) (e : (schemeSpace D).obj ≅ Limits.pullback v.hom a.hom) (dV : D ⟶ V) (dW : D ⟶ W), e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.fst v.hom a.hom = (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map dV ∧ (e.hom ≫ φ.hom) ≫ Limits.pullback.fst w.hom i.hom = (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map dW ∧ IsAffineHom dV.left ∧ ∃ (Q : Over B) (jV : V ⟶ Q) (jW : W ⟶ Q), IsPushout dV.left dW.left jV.left jW.left ∧ ∃ q : schemeSpace Q ⟶ P, (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map jV ≫ q.hom = v.hom ≫ j.hom ∧ (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map jW ≫ q.hom = w.hom ≫ b.hom ∧ IsEtale q.hom.hom ∧ IsSurjective q.hom.hom ∧ ∀ q' : schemeSpace Q ⟶ P, (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map jV ≫ q'.hom = v.hom ≫ j.hom → (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B).yoneda.map jW ≫ q'.hom = w.hom ≫ b.hom → q' = q
